Recent work supports studying semantic alignment and embedding geometry, but the search found no direct validation of training-only, scratch-trained title/description supervision for NextItNet. CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024) aligns pretrained description embeddings with collaborative representations through contrastive learning; its reliance on external language-model weights prevents direct adoption here. It motivates an auxiliary alignment objective, without establishing that a lightweight encoder trained from scratch will help. [CLA-Rec](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/).

Representation concentration deserves measurement, not an automatic collapse diagnosis. UniT (2025) reports semantic clustering in text-based sequential recommendation and proposes general, sequence-aware and popularity-aware pair sampling to improve uniformity. Conversely, an ICLR 2025 non-contrastive study finds that alignment can matter more than uniformity in sparse settings. These findings argue against indiscriminately repelling semantically related items or optimizing isotropy alone. [UniT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13530), [non-contrastive study](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/2d2f85c0f93e69cf71f58eebaebb5e8d-Abstract-Conference.html).

A compatible experimental hypothesis: retain one causal-convolution NextItNet per category and jointly train a small token-embedding/mean-pooling encoder over available titles/descriptions, with weak item–text contrastive alignment or auxiliary token prediction. Discard the auxiliary branch at inference; deploy the trained NextItNet alone. Ablate auxiliary weight zero, titles only, titles plus descriptions, and shuffled item–text assignments to distinguish useful correspondence from generic regularization. Track effective rank, cosine similarities and popularity-stratified validation performance alongside macro HR@10. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated results; no reviewed evidence establishes gains under the pinned benchmark.
